takeaway: Still dry, sunny and hot. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has a clear Wednesday on the North Pacific with a few gusts and Nicoya near 35°C. No rain is expected at the beach for the next two weeks. For surf, the Caribbean trades stay offshore at Nosara. Today is the last lighter day, so surf early. From late tonight the trades come back hard and now look to stay strong through Sunday, a day longer than yesterday's call. A new south-southwest swell shows up around Friday. No tropical storm threat and no rainy spell near Costa Rica.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Wed Nov 25 – Fri Nov 27)
periods.pattern: Dry air keeps skies clear. IMN calls the North Pacific clear to partly cloudy today, with occasional gusts early, moderate wind in the hills this afternoon, and wind picking up tonight. The Papagayo winds are light today, north to northeast around 10 knots. Late tonight they jump to about 25 knots off the Gulf of Papagayo and hold at 20–25 knots Thursday and Friday. A cold front stalls over northern Central America and boosts the trades, but it won't reach Costa Rica. The extra wind pushes rain onto the Caribbean side: the European and AI ensemble averages show their heaviest rain of the run on the Caribbean coast of Costa Rica and Panama in the 24 hours ending Friday evening. Every model keeps Nicoya at a trace or less.
periods.implications: Sunny and hot: about 35°C at Nicoya, low 30s at the beach, about 22°C at night. Today is the calm, sticky day. Thursday and Friday turn windy and dusty. Great for outdoor plans. Bring sun protection and water, not rain gear.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Sat Nov 28 – Tue Dec 1)
periods.pattern: The strong trades keep going. The marine forecast now holds northeast to east winds of 20–25 knots in the Papagayo area through Sunday, easing to about 20 knots off the gulf and 10–15 knots elsewhere Sunday night. All three ensemble averages and the main European model keep a strong east wind stream across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica through about Dec 1. IMN's weekly outlook (Nov 26–30) calls it stable and dry for the North Pacific, highs up to about 36°C, with only occasional mountain showers in the Northern Zone and Caribbean. Nicoya stays at a trace.
periods.implications: Windy and dusty Saturday and Sunday, calming slowly Monday and Tuesday. Boat and paddle trips are rough through Sunday. Tie down loose gear and be careful with fire. Rain at the beach is very unlikely.
periods.confidence: High on dry. Moderate-high on how strong the weekend wind gets.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Wed Dec 2 – Wed Dec 9)
periods.pattern: Classic dry season. The ensemble averages keep a steady east wind across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica all the way to Dec 9, a bit weaker after about Dec 5. IMN's monthly outlook (Nov 30–Dec 27) says the dry season is now set across the whole Pacific side, with 0–50 mm of rain a week on the North Pacific, a low chance of extreme rain, temperatures 3–3.5°C above normal, moderate wind the first week of December and very light wind with a very dry air mass after that. The US ensemble shows a weak low far offshore, well southwest of Guatemala and Costa Rica, around Dec 3–9. It stays far out at sea and the wind over Costa Rica stays easterly. The European and AI ensembles don't show it. A US global tropics outlook updated Nov 24 gives a 20–40% chance of a late-season tropical storm forming in early December, but far out in the open Pacific, more than 1,500 miles west of Costa Rica.
periods.implications: Plan freely. Sunny, breezy days through about Dec 5, then calmer, hotter and stickier. Dec 6 onward looks like the best stretch for boat trips. Yesterday's faint Dec 8 rain hint is now a far-offshore feature, not a Nosara concern.
periods.confidence: High on dry. Moderate on day-to-day wind strength after Dec 5.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trade winds (northeast to east), offshore at Nosara, for the whole period. Light today, strong from late tonight through Sunday, then easing slowly. No Pacific onshore pattern in sight. After about Dec 6 the trades get light, so the afternoon sea breeze takes over earlier.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued about 3:50 a.m. Costa Rica time) has north to northeast winds around 10 knots today. Late tonight it reaches about 25 knots off the Gulf of Papagayo and 15–20 knots elsewhere, then holds at 20–25 knots Thursday through Sunday. Off Nicoya and to the south, winds stay light and variable (under 5 knots), with a light northwest sea breeze around 10 knots this afternoon. So the offshore breeze reaches Nosara over the land, not along the coast, and today the sea breeze will turn it side-on fairly early. Swell (open-ocean numbers, not beach heights): south to southwest 4–6 ft at 16 seconds today and Thursday, a southwest pulse at 17 seconds Thursday night, building to 6–8 ft at 15 seconds Friday and 5–7 ft over the weekend. The big wave numbers in the Papagayo forecast from Thursday on are wind chop blowing out of the gulf, not surf for Nosara. Nicaragua is likely offshore mostly in the morning today, then all day Thursday through Sunday. That points to clean Nosara mornings, not all-day offshore here. Tides are still big just after the full moon, easing through the week.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today: dawn to mid-morning. Thursday Nov 26 to Sunday Nov 29: dawn to late morning, possibly past noon, but strong and gusty. Friday's new swell plus strong offshore looks like the pick. Monday Nov 30 to about Dec 5: dawn to late morning. From about Dec 6: early mornings only, as the trades fade.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore mornings. Moderate on afternoon sea-breeze timing and how long the offshore holds today.

gyreWatch.status: Not established. No watch needed. No prolonged rainy spell expected.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Nothing organized near Costa Rica through about Dec 9. The US hurricane center expects no storm formation in the eastern Pacific in the next 7 days near Central America (its only system is far away in the central Pacific). The global tropics outlook updated Nov 24 flags a 20–40% chance of a storm in early December, but far west in the open Pacific, not near Central America.
gyreWatch.supporting: Very little. The US ensemble's weak low far offshore around Dec 3–9 is the only hint, and the other ensembles don't show it. The tropics outlook notes upper-level conditions over the Americas may turn a bit more favorable for storms in weeks 2–3.
gyreWatch.conflicting: Strong trades all week, an east wind over Costa Rica in every ensemble through Dec 9, a strong El Niño, and IMN's call for a very dry December with very light wind after the first week all point to dry weather in Nosara.

whatChanged: The strong-trade stretch got longer: 20–25 knots in the Papagayo area now runs through Sunday instead of easing Saturday night, and starts late tonight. The next south-southwest swell now looks like Friday, not late tonight. The US global tropics outlook updated (Nov 24) and now flags a possible late-season storm in early December, but far out in the open Pacific. Yesterday's faint Dec 8 rain hint near the coast has moved offshore in today's US ensemble. IMN forecasts are unchanged: dry. Still no storms near Costa Rica.
practical: Surf early today, before mid-morning. Today is the best boat or paddle day until about Monday. Expect strong wind and dust Thursday through Sunday, with rough water. Plan outdoor events freely through early December. Stay hydrated, avoid open burning, and watch the still-big tides.
